title: A locally constant primitive for l-adic translation
statement: Let l be prime, s a nonnegative integer and M an additive commutative group killed by l^s. For every locally constant f:Z_l -> M [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] there is a locally constant h:Z_l -> M with h(x+1)-h(x)=f(x) for every x.

source.place: Second and third paragraphs, finite-quotient factorization and the periodic partial sums

proof.text: Give M the discrete topology. The open-normal-stabilizer theorem supplies an open subgroup U fixing f under right translation. Choose r with the ball of norm at most l^(-r) contained in U. Then f(n+l^r)=f(n) on integers. For reduction q modulo l^(r+s), x minus the canonical lift of q(x) has norm at most l^(-(r+s)), hence belongs to U; consequently f(q(x).val)=f(x).

Write L=l^r and N=l^(r+s)=L*l^s. Induction on the number of periods, splitting finite sums into consecutive blocks, gives sum_{n<N} f(n)=l^s times sum_{n<L} f(n)=0. For a in Z/NZ let H(a)=sum_{n<a.val} f(n). Away from the last residue the difference H(a+1)-H(a) is f(a.val). At the last residue the zero total sum gives the same equation across wraparound. This also applies when N=1.

Reduction modulo N is locally constant: the norm bound characterizing its kernel gives an open ball on which reduction is constant. Pull H back along reduction to obtain locally constant h. The cyclic difference equation and the preceding factorization give h(x+1)-h(x)=f(x).
